clue.text: Apart from husband

definitions.meaning: a verb meaning to use sparingly, conserve resources

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: 'save' means except, and to husband resources is to economise with them.

clue.text: Turned and drove into some thing, being drunk

definitions.text: Turned and drove into some thing
definitions.meaning: describes fixing a screw: twisting it into wood

explanation.definitionFit: A screw is twisted in, and 'screwed' is also British slang for very drunk.

clue.text: Man given short measure

indicators.note: short means the dance word loses its last letter

parts.note: a valeta is an old-time round dance, and measure is an old word for a dance

explanation.surface: A man cheated by being given a small measure of drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'measure' here is a dance, not a quantity.
explanation.definitionFit: A valet is a manservant, a gentleman's personal attendant.

clue.text: Reluctant to give fortune to husband

parts.note: one's lot is one's fortune or destiny

explanation.surface: Someone unwilling to hand over a fortune to their husband.
explanation.definitionFit: An older spelling of 'loath', meaning unwilling.

clue.text: Soldiers' condescend to listen to command

parts.note: OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

indicators.note: listen to signals we want the sound of the word, not its spelling

parts.note: to deign is to condescend

explanation.surface: Soldiers condescending to hear an order.
explanation.definitionFit: To ordain is to decree or order officially.

clue.text: Accommodating chap, needing to stay in other parts

indicators.note: the verb sits in the rearranged word
parts is read as a verb, splitting and reordering the letters of the word before it

parts.note: taken as written
to lie is to stay or remain, as in lie low

explanation.surface: A host who has to stay elsewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parts' rearranges the five letters to HOTER; 'in' places the verb before its last letter. 'Accommodating' looks like 'obliging' but means providing rooms.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotelier runs a hotel, providing guests with accommodation.

clue.text: Drink off better part of two pints — fine opening to festivities

indicators.note: the better part is more than half, so the end of the measure word is dropped here

parts.note: a quart is two pints
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads

indicators.note: the opening of the word festivities is its first letter

explanation.surface: A party-goer downing most of a quart as the festivities begin.
explanation.definitionFit: To quaff is to drink deeply, to swig a drink down.

clue.text: Doubt young man's title — he's a poser

parts.note: to question something is to doubt it
Master is the formal title for a boy

explanation.surface: Challenging a youth's right to be called by his title.
explanation.definitionFit: A quizmaster poses questions, so he is literally a poser of them.

clue.text: Hate Manitoba — moving East

indicators.note: moving the letters around rearranges them

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who loathes the Canadian province and moves east.
explanation.walkthrough: Manitoba is a Canadian prairie province.
explanation.definitionFit: To abominate is to loathe intensely.

clue.text: Expression of disgust about head's artfulness

indicators.note: the exclamation goes about the second piece

parts.note: fie is an old exclamation of disgust
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness's neighbour Sheerness

explanation.surface: Disgust at someone's skilful manipulation.
explanation.definitionFit: Finesse is delicate skill or subtlety in handling a situation.

clue.text: Unplayable ball. may start to move about

definitions.text: Unplayable ball. may start to move about

parts.words: Unplayable ball. may start to move about
parts.note: in cricket an unplayable delivery may disturb the wooden posts of the wicket, and the idiom means to get moving

explanation.walkthrough: Stumps are the three upright sticks of a cricket wicket; an unplayable ball hits them.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to get going, and stumps are what a cricket ball knocks over.

clue.text: Told lie — embarrassed about its rejection

indicators.note: the colour word is wrapped about the other piece

parts.note: an embarrassed person goes red

indicators.note: rejection here means turning the word for lie back on itself, read right to left

parts.note: a tale is a lie, a made-up story

explanation.surface: Someone told a lie, and blushes as it is disbelieved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'its rejection' sends the story word backwards, giving ELAT. 'Told' looks like part of the surface story; it is the definition, past tense of relate.
explanation.definitionFit: Related, as of a story, means recounted or narrated.

clue.text: Establish precisely why collar is untidy?

definitions.meaning: to pin down or fix definitely, as in settling the details of a plan
a playful reading: a neckwear item that has slipped makes the collar look scruffy

explanation.definitionFit: To tie down a fact is to pin it precisely, and a slipped tie is literally down.

clue.text: Where Tulliver worked, processing raw millet

indicators.note: processing grain reworks it, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A miller at work, grinding unprocessed grain.
explanation.walkthrough: Mr Tulliver is the miller in George Eliot's novel The Mill on the Floss.
explanation.definitionFit: Tulliver ran Dorlcote Mill, a water-driven grinding mill on the river.

clue.text: Arrange about introducing one to some small groups.

indicators.note: the numeral is introduced into the middle of the reversed word
about here means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to sort is to arrange
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Instructions for putting people into small groups.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns SORT into TROS, and 'introducing' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Trios are sets of three, the smallest groups beyond pairs.

clue.text: Guess you'll have to eat around either four or six

indicators.note: the meal word goes around the numeral

parts.note: to dine is to eat
VI is six in Roman numerals; IV, four, placed one letter earlier gives the same result

explanation.surface: A dinner riddle about what number to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: Clever: D(VI)INE and D(IV)INE both give the same letters, so either numeral works.
explanation.definitionFit: To divine is to guess by intuition.

clue.text: Abuse of instrument -not replace able, if I should break it

parts.note: a viola is a stringed instrument

indicators.note: the letter I breaks into the rearranged word
a word whose letters can be put back in a different place is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Mistreating an irreplaceable instrument by breaking it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replace able' rearranges NOT to TON, and I breaks in to make TION.
explanation.definitionFit: A violation is a breach or abuse of rules or rights.

clue.text: Devastated as engagement's broken by retiring-miss

indicators.note: the appointment word is split open by the other piece

parts.note: a date is an engagement or appointment

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: to miss something is to lose it

explanation.surface: Someone heartbroken when a shy woman calls off the engagement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' sends the loss word backwards, giving ESOL. 'Miss' looks like a young woman, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Desolate, as an adjective, means laid waste or utterly miserable.

clue.text: Almost support gold measure, in which one's gambling against the bank

definitions.text: in which one's gambling against the bank

indicators.note: almost means the support word loses its last letter

parts.note: to back is to support
a carat measures the purity of gold

explanation.surface: Backing a gold measure in a casino game.
explanation.definitionFit: Baccarat is a card game where players bet against the banker.

clue.text: Part of one's goal, to negotiate navigational hazard

parts.note: to negotiate an obstacle is to cross it
a bar is a sandbank across a harbour mouth

explanation.surface: A sailor's aim of getting past a dangerous sandbank.
explanation.definitionFit: The crossbar is the horizontal beam of the goal frame in football.

clue.text: Music-maker provides a select arrangement

indicators.note: a musical arrangement reorders, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A musician produces a choice arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A celesta is a keyboard instrument with bell-like tones.

clue.text: Appearance in a southern French city

indicators.note: the bearing word sits inside the other two pieces

parts.note: mien is a person's appearance or bearing

explanation.surface: Someone shows up in a city in southern France.
explanation.definitionFit: Amiens is a city in northern France, capital of the Somme department.

clue.text: Unusual way to' replace good. opening in country house

indicators.note: the street abbreviation replaces the opening letter of the house word

parts.note: a grange is a country house with farm buildings
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: An odd way to replace the door of a country house.
explanation.definitionFit: Strange means odd or out of the ordinary.

clue.text: Run into card-game from which one can bring home the bacon

definitions.text: from which one can bring home the bacon

indicators.note: the abbreviation goes into the card game

parts.note: poker is a card game
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A gambler who brings home the winnings from a card game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bring home the bacon' means earn money, but here bacon is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A porker is a pig fattened for meat, so it yields bacon.

clue.text: Securing article, in case as small as possible

indicators.note: the conjunction holds the article firmly inside it

parts.note: lest means in case, for fear that
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Fastening an item inside a case to keep it small.
explanation.definitionFit: Least is the superlative of little, the smallest amount possible.

clue.text: Angry about mixing musical styles

parts.note: cross means angry
over can mean about, concerning, as in a row over money

explanation.surface: Someone furious at a fusion of musical genres.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossover music blends genres, such as classical with pop.

clue.text: Seats I've returned, having restricted view like this

indicators.note: returned says the hidden letters are read backwards
having means containing, so the letters are held within the words that precede

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone who handed back their theatre seats because the view was restricted.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition swallowed 'having', the only signal for the concealed run; 'having' holds ATSIV, which 'returned' turns round, and a vista is a framed, restricted view.
explanation.definitionFit: A vista is a long narrow view, framed and restricted by trees or buildings.

clue.text: Wife comes in to cook fish, for example

indicators.note: the abbreviation enters the cooking word

parts.note: to simmer is to cook gently

explanation.surface: A wife arrives to prepare some fish for dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fish' looks like the dish being cooked; here it is the verb, one who swims.
explanation.definitionFit: A fish is an example of a creature that swims.

clue.text: Back smooth working of part of ship

indicators.note: back means the word for smooth is written backwards

parts.note: sleek means smooth
on means working, operating

explanation.surface: Smoothing the back as part of a ship's hull is worked on.
explanation.definitionFit: A keelson is the timber or girder fixed along a ship's keel to strengthen it.

clue.text: A long time to fix name for her?

indicators.note: the abbreviation is fixed inside the time word

parts.note: ages means a long time

explanation.surface: It took ages to decide what to call her.
explanation.definitionFit: Agnes is a woman's name, so it can stand for 'her'.

clue.text: High water sailor spotted 'before noon

indicators.note: the sailor word comes before the abbreviation

parts.note: tar is a traditional word for a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor spots a lake in the hills before midday.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarn is a small mountain lake, water found high up.

clue.text: Maltreat freshmen? It's not clear

definitions.meaning: to subject new students to humiliating initiation, a US college custom
a mist or fog that obscures the view

explanation.definitionFit: Hazing is the bullying of newcomers, and a haze is a mist that blurs things.
